findings.Quote: He was a man trying to swim in air.
findings.Note: Purple metaphor that doesn't hold literal scrutiny — swimming in air doesn't clearly convey fumbling with a gun, it's decorative rather than clarifying.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with concrete physical description: 'His arm wove like the signal was arriving late.'

findings.Quote: Tomas knew the signs the way a man knows weather.
findings.Note: Stock simile for reading someone's condition; adds no specificity.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile and show one concrete tell instead.

findings.Quote: the way everything cost him something now that there was nothing in the door pocket to pay with but himself
findings.Note: purple, abstract metaphor that doesn't hold up to literal scrutiny — unclear what 'paying with himself' concretely means in this moment
findings.Fix: replace with a concrete physical or behavioral detail showing the cost

findings.Quote: He'd filed the form himself that morning, before the Ward, before any of it.
findings.Note: Contradicts later description that he sat with the unsent reason text 'the rest of the day' after typing it, and that 'the night had happened' before he sent it — but he supposedly filed it that morning, meaning the decision to return preceded the events (the Ward, the night) that reportedly caused his change of heart, undermining the causal logic of the redemption arc.
findings.Fix: clarify that he pulled the organ that morning but only decided/drafted the return reason later, after the night's events

findings.Quote: she had looked at him through the channel the way you'd look at a dog that has tried to explain something, waiting, faintly, for the sound to stop
findings.Note: Overworked simile stacks abstraction on abstraction (dog explaining itself, waiting for sound to stop) without a clear literal image; strains believability of what a look can convey.
findings.Fix: Simplify to a single concrete beat, e.g. 'She'd looked at him the way you look at a dog that's learned to sit — waiting for the trick to end.'

findings.Quote: true was the only lie that never slipped
findings.Note: Aphoristic quip that reads as authorial cleverness rather than Tomas's lived reasoning; slows the pressure moment.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause or replace with a concrete detail about his control of his face.

findings.Quote: It was just what the early shift smelled like.
findings.Note: Flat filler line restating the preceding sentence without adding new information.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence; the refrigerator simile already lands the point.

findings.Quote: the way you stop hearing a refrigerator
findings.Note: Familiar desensitization simile, low-cost but slightly worn.
findings.Fix: Swap for a sensory detail specific to this world instead of a generic domestic comparison.

findings.Quote: like a man carrying a cooler to a cookout he didn't want to attend
findings.Note: Incongruous, near-comic simile undercuts the grim institutional tone the beat is building.
findings.Fix: Replace with a flatter, colder image consistent with the scene's register.

findings.Quote: getting less surprised
findings.Note: Vague euphemism for dying that undercuts the visceral weight the beat needs at its turning point.
findings.Fix: State it plainly: 'the surprise going out of them.'

findings.Quote: the flat failed on him mid-word
findings.Note: stock 'voice cracking under emotion' beat dressed up in slightly odd phrasing, still a familiar telling-not-showing move
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a concrete physical detail (a pause, a repeated word) rather than naming the failure

findings.Quote: the way a man goes quiet when he understands he's seen too much
findings.Note: generalizing aphorism that tells the reader how to interpret Osei's stillness instead of showing it
findings.Fix: cut the explanatory clause and let the stillness stand on its own

findings.Quote: his voice did the one warm thing it knew how to do, the thing it did when it wanted something
findings.Note: double-hedged telling construction that explains Levin's manipulation rather than dramatizing it
findings.Fix: trim to one clause, e.g. 'his voice went warm, the way it did when it wanted something'

findings.Quote: which was its own kind of message, and Levin had enough of his native intelligence left under the drug to receive it
findings.Note: tells the reader Levin understood rather than showing the understanding land
findings.Fix: cut the explanatory clause; the silence already conveys it

findings.Quote: "They're not a gang, they're a church, and what they worship is blood."
findings.Note: vivid but slightly overwrought aphorism risks tipping into stock 'crime family as religion' shorthand rather than delivering concrete political stakes the beat purpose demands
findings.Fix: follow immediately with a concrete mechanism (already partially done) or trim the line to reduce its aphoristic weight

findings.Quote: a weight settling in the chest he didn't argue with
findings.Note: vague interiority-telling for a hardened character's reaction, generic emotional shorthand
findings.Fix: replace with a specific physical action or omit

findings.Quote: A man tells you more while he can still watch you decide what to take next.
findings.Note: aphoristic authorial intrusion that reads as a stated 'universal truth' about torture rather than character observation
findings.Fix: cut or attribute directly to Tomas's specific reasoning about this scene

findings.Quote: Real knight in shining armor.
findings.Note: Sarcastic quip lands as filler wit rather than character-specific voice, slightly softening the grim mechanics of the discovery.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a flatter, more procedural line of contempt.

findings.Quote: the glass behind his eyes was thin, worn down to a man instead of a mood
findings.Note: Purple, vague interiority metaphor that doesn't hold up to literal scrutiny (glass 'worn down to a man' is incoherent imagery).
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete physical tell of Levin's fatigue/vulnerability.

findings.Quote: That landed harder than an argument would have.
findings.Note: Tells the reader the emotional effect instead of letting the preceding beat (Levin's flat acceptance) demonstrate it.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence; the dialogue already shows the weight.

findings.Quote: He'd crossed some line tonight where the drug had stopped being the answer.
findings.Note: Tells the reader the crisis threshold has been crossed instead of letting the preceding physical details carry it — redundant summary after strong show-don't-tell work.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence; let the capped vial and unspoken beat carry the meaning.

findings.Quote: They came to the edges and waited.
findings.Note: Slightly generic horror-atmosphere phrasing that trades precision for mood, weaker than the specific images around it (the eyeless man, the kid sitting back down).
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a more specific, non-generic image tied to Levin's actual hallucinations.

findings.Quote: Men do, and then they don't.
findings.Note: Aphoristic filler — a pseudo-profound generalization that doesn't add information beyond 'he eventually talked.'
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence; move directly to 'Somewhere in the long middle of it he'd given up two men...'

findings.Quote: a man who read sins off coats would notice
findings.Note: Slightly overwrought turn of phrase for describing the hunter's method, a bit purple compared to the plain register around it.
findings.Fix: Simplify to something like 'a man who noticed one clean door among dirty ones.'

findings.Quote: The wind came off the water flat and cold and asked him for nothing. That was the strange part. Everything else in his life had always asked him for something.
findings.Note: Personifying the wind as 'asking for nothing' followed by an explanatory aphorism tells the reader the meaning instead of trusting the image.
findings.Fix: Cut the explanatory second sentence and let the wind image stand alone, or replace with a more concrete physical detail of relief.

findings.Quote: he felt it the way you feel a fire once you're far enough away that it's only warmth on your back
findings.Note: Duplicated near-verbatim in beat 2, undercutting its intended freshness and reading as a stock distancing metaphor.
findings.Fix: Use only once across the two beats, or differentiate the image significantly.

findings.Quote: Levin kept it to prove there'd been a before. For years he'd kept it the way you keep a thing you can't bear to look at. Now he looked at it, at the light, with his sick clean shaking hands.
findings.Note: the beat's purpose is the turn from looking away to looking — the actual moment of looking is rushed and under-rendered compared to the setup, weakening the payoff the beat promises
findings.Fix: slow down the moment of looking itself, give it more weight than the summary of past avoidance

findings.Quote: Levin was a
findings.Note: sentence cuts off mid-thought, an apparent truncation error
findings.Fix: complete the sentence describing Levin's position/action

findings.Quote: You couldn't unmake a man who'd been made to track. You could only point him, or let the skill rot in him like meat left in the sun.
findings.Note: Aphoristic double-metaphor reads as authorial commentary rather than character interiority; the meat-in-sun image is a stretch for 'skill rotting.'
findings.Fix: Cut to one image or ground it in a specific memory rather than general truism.

findings.Quote: Not hunger — he'd never named it hunger. Just the click of a made thing finding the work it was made for.
findings.Note: Tips into telling-not-showing his psychology with a mechanical metaphor that asserts depth rather than earning it in-scene.
findings.Fix: Trim to action: cut the aphoristic aside and let the investigative competence itself imply his nature.

findings.Quote: the way another man squares a stack of paper before he leaves a desk
findings.Note: Explanatory simile that tells us the meaning of the ritual instead of trusting the folded handkerchief image already established.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile, end on 'wanting the day to have an edge.'

findings.Quote: It wasn't a signature. It was just his hands, wanting the day to have an edge.
findings.Note: Purpose states the handkerchief 'establishes his ritual orderliness as a character signature,' but the prose explicitly denies it is a signature, undercutting the stated beat purpose.
findings.Fix: Remove the denial or rephrase so the ritual is affirmed as characteristic rather than disclaimed.

findings.Quote: He had done that.
findings.Note: Short, isolated declarative sentence used for dramatic weight is a familiar rhythmic tic that reads as stock gravitas rather than earned insight.
findings.Fix: Integrate the realization into the surrounding paragraph or replace with a more specific, concrete admission of consequence.

findings.Quote: he felt it the way you feel a fire once you're far enough away that it's only warmth on your back
findings.Note: This simile appears verbatim in beat 3 as well as being echoed here almost identically, making it a retread rather than a fresh image within this beat.
findings.Fix: Vary the image or cut the repetition between beats.

findings.Quote: Nobody said anything for a moment that had a whole life in it.
findings.Note: Vague, self-consciously portentous phrasing that tells us the moment is heavy without showing why.
findings.Fix: Cut to a concrete beat: describe a breath held, a hand's stillness, or simply hold the silence without editorializing.

findings.Quote: the way, Tomas would understand later, he laid it when he wanted you to know he wasn't, yet, reaching for it
findings.Note: The 'would understand later' foreshadowing construction is a stock suspense device bordering on 'little did he know.'
findings.Fix: Drop the flash-forward framing; render the observation as Tomas's immediate read of the gesture.

findings.Quote: the order thirty years had taught him to take a story out of a body
findings.Note: tells the reader Tomas's expertise via exposition rather than letting the specific observations alone demonstrate it
findings.Fix: cut the explanatory clause; the eyes/mouth/hands sequence already shows the method

findings.Quote: the smell of a tank that had kept cycling after it had nothing left to repair
findings.Note: morbid-poetic flourish bordering on overwrought scene-dressing, slightly redundant with the preceding sentence which already states the same idea
findings.Fix: cut one of the two redundant clauses describing the nanite bath smell

findings.Quote: the way a man speaks when he's holding something he isn't sure won't break
findings.Fix: cut the simile or replace with a concrete physical detail specific to Levin

findings.Quote: He looked like a man waiting for a knock he wasn't sure was coming.
findings.Fix: replace with a more specific, less generic image tied to Levin's particular guilt

findings.Quote: You learned their border the way you learned weather — not from a forecast, but from the ache in a joint that had been broken once already.
findings.Note: Purple simile that strains under scrutiny — weather isn't learned from a broken joint's ache, the comparison muddles rather than clarifies.
findings.Fix: Cut to: 'You learned their border the way a broken bone learns weather — early, and without being told twice.'

findings.Quote: a little schism, months old, the neighborhood stepping around it like a puddle it had stopped resenting
findings.Note: Overwrought personification stacked on personification ('stopped resenting') that tells us mood rather than showing concrete detail.
findings.Fix: Simplify: 'a little schism, months old, the neighborhood just walked around now.'

findings.Quote: a turnstile that hadn't taken his fare
findings.Note: Mechanical simile that undercuts the tension with a cute, over-worked image at the story's most dangerous beat.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile; just describe the physical stop.

findings.Quote: He was, whatever else the night had made of him, a professional.
findings.Note: Stock 'whatever else X, he was a professional' construction that tells rather than shows the discipline the beat is meant to demonstrate.
findings.Fix: Cut the line; let the coffee purchase carry the professionalism.
